newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity prices rise on weather, natgas.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity prices rise on weather, natgas.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading higher Wednesday on forecasts of above-normal temperatures in the U.S. West and in sympathy with higher natural gas prices, industry sources said.
Forecasts called for mild temperatures through much of the West through the weekend, with expecations of cooling demand particularily in areas of the Southwest, the sources said.
Also, natural gas prices were said to be exerting some psychological pressure, with May NYMEX Henry Hub futures trading up 3.8 cents at $1.975 per million British thermal units as of 1220 EDT.

May Palo Verde (PV) electricity futures were trading up 31 cents as of 1220 EDT at the day's high of $16.20 per megawatt hour (MWh) after exchange as low as $15.95, while June was up 32 cents at $17.25 after reaching as low as $17.00 per MWh.
May California Oregon Border (COB) was up 24 cents at $12.85 after trade as low as $12.80, while June was up 16 cents at $12.45 after exchange as low as $12.30 per MWh.
Weather was said to be having a particular impact on Palo Verde futures due to calls for some much above-normal weather over the next week.
In the Southwest, temperatures were expected to be three to 15 degrees above normal with dry conditions through the weekend. Temperatures were seen returning to near-normal levels early next week.
Weather in the Pacific Northwest was forecast to be dry and mild through the weekend, averaging three to eight degrees above normal. Some possible precipitation was seen by Sunday.
Longer-term forecasts called for above-normal temperatures in the Pacific Northwest from April 20 to 24, with near normal temperatures in the northwest portion of the area during the same period.
NYMEX said that as of 1150 EDT an estimated total of 90 COB and 245 PV contracts had traded.

Separately, several generation units in the West returned to service earlier this week, including the 1,073 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon nuclear unit 2 in Avila Beach, Calif., the 1,212 MW Helms pumped storage hydroelectric plant near Fresno, Calif., and the 750 MW Navajo coal-fired power plant near Page, Ariz.,
COB open interest for April 15 rose 111 to 4,149 while PV open interest rose eight to 4,676, NYMEX said.
